title: Text on a coloured background
summary: color and background-color together, and why contrast decides whether it is readable.
explanation: color sets the text colour and background-color fills the box behind it. The two only work as a pair: what matters is the contrast between them.

The first two swatches are easy to read. The third, light grey on white, and the fourth, white on a mid orange, look fine at a glance but are hard to read for many people, especially on a phone in sunlight.
The same colour can be written several ways: #ea580c, rgb(234 88 12) and hsl(21 90% 48%) are all the same orange.
tryThis: Change .poor-grey's color to #52525b: much better contrast, still grey.
Give .poor-orange a darker background, #c2410c: the white text becomes readable.
Write .good-dark's background as hsl(240 6% 10%) instead of the hex value.

children.text: Light on dark: easy to read
Dark on light: easy to read
Light grey on white: hard to read
White on mid orange: hard to read
